title: Best Finance Options for New Build Homes
h1: Not revealed by snippets. Both searches list the page under the SERP/meta title 'Best Finance Options for New Build Homes'; the slug reads 'different-ways-to-finance-new-build-homes-in-the-uk'.
metaDescription: Not revealed verbatim. Search (a)'s excerpt says the page covers more options 'from self-build mortgages to government schemes', which reads like meta-description wording but is unconfirmed.
summary: Blog article (type: guide/listicle, not a case study) giving an overview of the main ways to fund a new-build home in the UK. Content actually revealed by snippets: (1) New build mortgages, described as 'generally standard mortgage products designed to fund properties that have recently been constructed or are currently being constructed'; lenders apply stricter criteria and lower loan-to-value ratios, with typical LTVs of 75% to 85%, and some lenders set deadlines for completion; the page appears to have a 'Key Features' subsection. (2) Self-build mortgages, for people building from scratch: 'Unlike a traditional mortgage, funds are released in stages' at construction milestones, either in arrears or in advance. (3) Buy-to-let mortgages for new builds, for investors buying a new-build property to rent out. The excerpt says the article covers further options 'from self-build mortgages to government schemes', so a government-schemes section exists but its content was not surfaced. Search (b)'s tool summary also described development finance (loan secured against land, released in tranches tied to the build schedule, interest rolled up and repaid on completion from sales or refinance, first tranche usually covering the land and generally not exceeding 75% of the purchase price), mezzanine finance and bridging loans, and exit routes (sell the units, rent and refinance, or repay from other developments), but it explicitly attributed the mezzanine/bridging points to the Scotland guide and drew on /property-development-finance/ and other sibling pages, so attribution of those points to this article is uncertain. The full article body (introduction, government schemes section, any conclusion or CTA) was not retrieved.
